title: Unified retry policy and safeguard patterns for multi-region failover and SDKs
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Standardize retry, timeout and backoff semantics across services and client SDKs to support SLO-driven multi-region failover, hedged requests, idempotency guarantees, and graceful load-shedding. This ticket defines the policy surface, SDK contract changes, server-side safety guards, and rollout/testing plan.
background: We currently have diverging retry implementations across services and SDKs: different default timeouts, exponential backoff variants, and idempotency handling. This causes inconsistent behavior during multi-region failover and makes hedged requests risky (duplicate side effects) unless idempotency is enforced. Recent incidents showed cascading retries increasing tail latency and tripping regional capacity fast; we need a unified, SLO-aware approach that prevents amplification while allowing fast, safe failover.
goals: Define a single canonical retry and timeout policy family for HTTP/gRPC and SDKs (server and client defaults)
Introduce an explicit idempotency header contract and server validation rules
Add support for hedged requests in SDKs with explicit opt-in and server-side duplicate suppression tracing
Implement circuit breaker and load-shedding defaults tunable by SLO tier and region capacity
Expose observability (histograms, traces, events) to reason about retries, hedges, and load-shedding decisions
constraints: Must be backward-compatible for existing customers unless they opt-in to the new behavior. Changes should be guarded by feature flags and rollout via runtime-1.20. SDK surface changes must be surfaced as opt-in first, then can flip defaults for new major SDK versions. No cross-region state assumptions — servers must make safe decisions with eventual consistency.
proposed_solution:
1) Retry Policy: publish a policy document with three tiers: Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive. Each tier defines max attempts, base timeout, per-call deadline, and capped exponential backoff jitter algorithm (caps both max backoff and total retry window).
  2) SLO-aware routing: client SDKs read per-route SLO metadata (from a light config blob at boot or via control-plane) and select retry tier automatically. If the route is latency-sensitive (SLO p99 <= 200ms), choose Conservative; for throughput-bound background tasks choose Balanced.
  3) Idempotency contract: introduce header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key (UUIDv4) with server-side 24h dedupe table for mutating endpoints. Servers respond with 409 when duplicate non-idempotent attempts detected or a canonical idempotent outcome. Document behavior for retries across regions (use request fingerprint + key).
  4) Hedged Requests: SDKs expose an opt-in API hedgedCall(fn, hedgeSettings). HedgeSettings include maxHedgeDelay and maxConcurrentHedges. Servers mark responses with X-Redwood-Hedge-Handled to indicate duplicate suppression. Hedged calls must require idempotency key for mutating ops.
  5) Circuit breakers and load shedding: deploy a default circuit breaker middleware with steady-state thresholds (error rate, latency spike, queue depth). Add a load-shedding tier that returns 429 with specific Retry-After and an error code "REDEMPTY" when service is under pressure; prefer shedding non-critical routes first.
  6) Telemetry: emit retry_attempt, hedge_sent, hedge_won, idempotency_duplicate_detected, shed_decision events to ingestion. Tag by route/model/region and include SLO tier to enable post-mortem and ML-driven tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical retry policy doc published in Confluence and linked from SDK READMEs
SDKs (js/py/go) implement retry tiers and hedgedCall with feature-flag gating
Server-side idempotency header implemented for top 10 mutating endpoints with dedupe cache and tests
Circuit breaker middleware enabled in runtime-1.20 can be toggled per-route and per-region
Dashboards show retry amplification ratio <= 1.5 during simulated failover and shed decisions are visible via events
Chaos test: simulate a region outage and verify clients fail over within SLO targets without spiking retries or causing more than 5% increase in global 5xx rate
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfood (canary tenants) with SDK opt-in hedging and server-side idempotency for critical endpoints. Phase 2: enable retry tiers as a feature-flag default for new routes and surface config in Console. Phase 3: flip defaults in major SDK release after 4 weeks stabilization and monitoring OK. Provide automatic rollback via feature flags and emergency kill-switch in control plane.
testing_plan: Unit tests for backoff math and jitter, integration tests for hedged calls behavior, end-to-end chaos tests that simulate region latency/failure while asserting SLOs, performance benchmark to ensure hedging doesn't add >2% median latency, and security review for idempotency key handling (sensitive data should not be captured).
metrics_and_alerting: p99 latency by region and route
5xx rate increase correlated with retry spikes
notes: Key trade-off: hedging speeds up failover but requires strong idempotency on servers to avoid duplicates. We will restrict hedging to readmost and explicitly idempotent mutating routes until dedupe guarantees are proven. Consider a light-weight global dedupe index for critical customers as an enterprise add-on later.
open_questions: What TTL is acceptable for server dedupe tables for customer workloads with long running async operations?
Should the idempotency key be honored cross-region or only within a single region to prevent cross-region conflicts?
How to version SDKs so that older clients remain safe when servers start enforcing idempotency headers?
blockers: Dependence on runtime feature flags infra (ENG-35671) and a perf-safe dedupe cache implementation. Security review for header handling must complete before canary.
